A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian reconstruction framework, renamed from UniG to UniGS. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Objaverse/GSO reconstruction experiments, timing measurements, component ablations, and qualitative generation results, including additional experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds single-image reconstruction comparisons, masking experiments, initialization sensitivity results, and further qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The UNet features, Gaussian-query decoder, MVDFA, SESA, coarse initialization, and MSE-plus-LPIPS objective remain. The coarse-to-fine explanation moves into Appendix A.1.2 as initialization; the rewritten description does not establish a changed algorithm or training procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds direct single-image reconstruction in Appendix A.3.4, Table 6, and Figure 19, distinct from v1's single-image pipeline using diffusion-generated additional views. Objaverse LVIS, GSO, fixed/random camera inputs, and diffusion-assisted generation coverage are otherwise retained.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds literature-reported GeoLRM, GRM, and GS-LRM results. New evaluations include Triplane-Gaussian and TripoSR in Table 6, MVSplat and masked MVSplat in Table 9, and masked LGM/Splatter Image in Table 7. Appendix A.3.7 also reports a qualitative assessment of pixelSplat.

E3.justification: The original data split, principal metrics, training budget, and main evaluation settings remain. Added protocols remove background Gaussians, vary initialization from one to four views while retaining four refinement views, extend inference testing to 16 views, and demonstrate resolution 512. These extend testing without establishing changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds background-masking controls investigating ghosting, per-view colored point-cloud diagnostics, initialization-view sensitivity, and extended view-count testing. The original SESA/Gaussian-count analysis is retained as Figure 6, formerly Figure 13. Conversely, the freezing ablation loses the separate coarse-frozen/encoder-finetuned condition from v1 Table 8.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix A.4 newly reports 10 experiments varying the selected initialization views and states that PSNR variance is within 0.185. v1 has no corresponding variability report. This does not establish repeated training seeds or uncertainty estimates for the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: Most matched original values remain unchanged, including 30.4245 fixed-view PSNR and 26.3020 random-view PSNR. New results include direct single-image PSNR of 23.45 versus TripoSR's 20.00 and Triplane-Gaussian's 18.61, masking outcomes, MVSplat comparisons, and initialization sensitivity. The 25.6902 PSNR freezing-ablation entry disappears. These are added or removed results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The additional numbered projection, sampling, fusion, and camera-coordinate equations restate mathematics already present in v1's prose or pseudocode. Gaussian parameter notation is revised, but neither version supplies new theoretical guarantees, assumptions, or proofs relative to the other.

C1.justification: v3 adds a prominent claim that unitary Gaussians concentrate more representation capacity in complex regions. Its contribution list emphasizes unitary world-space representation and MVDFA, while deemphasizing SESA and coarse-to-fine initialization. The central reconstruction, view-consistency, variable-view inference, and benchmark-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands interpretation: masking experiments attribute ghosting to cross-view misalignment rather than background points; additional discussion explains diminishing gains from redundant views and critiques triplane and scene-based alternatives. Initialization-view choice also receives a new rationale. The limitation requiring supplied camera parameters is retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents using the first camera as the reference coordinate frame and supplies an intended code-release address, without establishing that code is available. It removes v1's explicit disclosure that refinement training finetunes both the coarse stage and encoder. Most hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage expands substantially to recent reconstruction systems including GS-LRM, GRM, GeoLRM, pixelSplat, MVSplat, TripoSR, and Triplane-Gaussian. New discussion positions UniGS against voxel/triplane representations and scene-oriented Gaussian methods through differences in geometry, supervision, and computational cost.

P1.justification: The title and model name change, and the abstract, introduction, method exposition, experiments, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting and restructuring. Initialization moves to the appendix and deformable attention gains a dedicated introduction. v3 also retains the old related-work paragraphs before the revised Related Work section, creating substantial duplication.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn, the original variable-view plot is incorporated into Figure 1, and existing point-cloud, sensitivity, and generation figures move into the main text. New diagnostic, single-image, and high-resolution figures and comparison tables substantially expand the displays. Some captions are mismatched, notably Figure 17's caption for its view-count plot.

improvement.justification: The new masking controls and initialization-sensitivity study address unanswered questions in v1, while direct single-image and MVSplat evaluations broaden empirical support. These provide a limited net improvement. Benefits are tempered by duplicated related work, less explicit finetuning documentation, and the unchanged 4.2 dB headline, which is not reconciled with the stronger, differently configured baselines added to Table 1.
